While the dialogue is well-crafted and relies effectively on subtext, the story utilizes several well-worn romance and drama clichés. The setting itself—two estranged ex-lovers meeting in the rain in front of a closed café because one is "only in town for a short time"—is a classic, overused trope. Additionally, the story relies on predictable metaphorical exchanges, such as using the bitterness of the coffee to represent the bitterness of their past relationship, and using a literal action (Mara putting her cup down) to immediately trigger a metaphorical jab about her character flaws ("leaving things standing until someone else picks them up").
